newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cyclone warning for Western Australian coast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cyclone warning for Western Australian coast.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Meteorology on Monday issued a category one cyclone warning for coastal areas between Broome and Port Hedland in Western Australia.

"Gales with gusts to 100 kilometres per hour may develop on the coast between Broome and Wallal later today and could extend southwest to Port Hedland early Tuesday," the Western Australian office of the Bureau said.

At 5.00 a.m. (1800 GMT) Cyclone Rachel was estimated to be 110 kilometres west-northwest of Broome and 420 kilometres northeast of Port Hedland and moving southwest at 10 kilometres per hour parallel to the coast, it said.
Western Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET) operates the Barrow Island oilfield which is about 400 kilometres west of Port Hedland.
WAPET is a joint venture of Texaco Inc, Chevron Inc and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil Corp, with one-seventh.
Woodside Petroleum Ltd operates the North West shelf gas field which is also about 400-500 kilometres west of Port Hedland.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
